o1.biggest_strength: It correctly brings back the paused winning front-of-pack angle, adds the missing taste hook from reviews, and faces the ₹90-per-bar objection plainly.
o1.biggest_mistake: The six primary texts are not quite six distinct angles because transparency appears twice and there is no clean standalone protein or 4 pm snack execution.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Swap one repeated label-reader/transparency line for a sharper pure protein or 4 pm office-snack primary text while keeping the same level of product proof and character counts.

o2.biggest_strength: It nails the data signals: relaunches the tired winner, makes taste the main challenger, includes the price objection, and gives a practical launch test with sound arithmetic.
o2.biggest_mistake: A couple of lines, especially the taste line, could show more of what is inside the bar so they feel less like copy any protein bar could run.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add product proof to the taste-led copy and use the transparency headline in the first launch set without weakening the clean test design.

reason: Both are strong and usable, but Output 2 gives the cleaner six-angle set the owner hoped for: transparency, taste, no added sugar, protein/texture, 4 pm snack, and price. Output 1 is a touch more self-contained in individual lines, but it repeats angles more.
